feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete platforms, scope, and outcomes. It is generally clear and polished, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with some formatting inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support leadership in digital platforms, governance, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility and impact signals: examples like a 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Broad yet coherent skill set: strategy, CMS/web delivery, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are well aligned to the target brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition: NACo responsibilities and themes (web, email, social, video, governance) recur across multiple roles; condense older roles and emphasize distinct achievements/results.  
- Improve structure/readability: the “Recent Projects” content in the footer is valuable but oddly placed; move it into a dedicated “Selected Projects” section. Also reduce overlap between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.”  
- Fix style consistency: use consistent punctuation in lists (e.g., “social, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and video”), standardize capitalization (“DAVIS” vs normal title case), and consider “A2 (learning)” instead of “A2/Learning.” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground public-sector scale/results.
- Replace generic phrasing like “building the platforms” with more direct action verbs such as “leading” or “modernizing.”
- Consider adding one concrete scope marker (for example, enterprise websites, multi-channel operations, or large publisher environments) to increase specificity.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads digital strategy across website modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” and the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” are somewhat repetitive.
- The list of capabilities closely mirrors Core Competencies; keep the intro higher-level to avoid duplication.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it feel more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording for faster scanning.
- Replace broader items with sharper, higher-value terms tied to recent work and leadership scope.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, consider “content discovery” over “content experiences,” which is more specific and better aligned with the AI search project.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled search…” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This section also overlaps with Topline Skills; keep Core Competencies high-level and let Topline Skills carry tools/platform detail.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats accomplishments already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and context.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Built/Developed/Launched…” plus platform, audience, or business result.
- Replace generic terms like “improve discovery” and “continued campaign growth” with measurable outcomes if available.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with current/previous NACo bullets; consider making this a “Selected Projects” block with only projects not fully described elsewhere.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item here; prioritize similarly unique examples to avoid repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant recent role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles by emphasizing consultant scope, platform modernization, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, Drupal platform enhancements, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Designed cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics processes to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Reframe technical execution with outcomes: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsites, and member toolkits; provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for public-facing properties.”
- Make the AI/search bullet more specific if possible: add scope or result, e.g., “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX for policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current governance, analytics, and digital systems language overlaps heavily with the Director of Digital Media entry.
- Microsite/campaign examples are already reinforced in Recent Projects, so keep this item higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and the bullets emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and enterprise change over channel coverage.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a tighter scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for channels/studio/analytics: email engagement growth, production cost savings, faster reporting cycles, improved publishing compliance, reduced vendor reliance.
- Combine lower-value operational bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Established governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning processes to improve consistency, speed and accountability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program growth appears elsewhere; here, emphasize building the in-house studio and strategic capacity shift.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, repeatability, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + outcome: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial and advocacy operations during a period of organizational growth.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: newsletters, video program, editorial coordination, workflow improvement.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: subscriber counts, send volume/open rates, video cadence/views, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Possible rewrite:
- Managed NACo’s daily digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving coordination of editorial and advocacy content.
- Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on scaling/operationalizing the program.
- “Publishing workflows” and “coordination” also appear in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating governance language.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and outcomes-adjacent strengths rather than broad communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications systems leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Prefer “systems,” “operations,” and “governance” over “messaging” to better match the recent leadership roles.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise web strategy for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”
- Keep terminology aligned with the header and recent experience; avoid softer phrasing like “content planning” when “content operations” is more senior and distinctive.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo entries and reads less differentiated than the stronger platform/operations themes.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps with the Technical + IT section. It should emphasize the platforms and execution strengths most supported by recent experience, especially Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to a tighter, impact-oriented grouping: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint, WordPress and Power Pages • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and keep it dominant; it is the clearest platform match to the most recent roles and projects.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, swap “CMS modernization” for “enterprise CMS modernization” to better match the scale shown elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially repeats “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and avoid listing too many individual tools.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so mention it here only if you trim overlap elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize business impact and decision support.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & reporting: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI and BigQuery; KPI framework development, executive dashboarding, leadership reporting, and SEO/performance analysis.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. “supporting enterprise web optimization and strategic decision-making.”
- Keep only the most decision-oriented terms here; let the Technical + IT section carry the full tool inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; avoid repeating the exact same tool list in both places.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use one to stress strategy, the other tools.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational scope and higher-value delivery rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward outcomes and level: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to signal seniority and align with the in-house studio achievement.
- Replace “Livestreaming” with “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” for clearer event relevance.
- If space allows, add one stronger systems phrase: “Studio buildout and operations” or “Multimedia production workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- Tool-level detail like PTZ/studio operations may be redundant with “Multimedia & Creative Tools” unless this skill block is meant to show delivery capability, not software.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest recent platform in your experience, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling strength: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of more platforms: **Drupal (migration, governance, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep this item platform-only; avoid adding “CMS modernization” or implementation terms already covered elsewhere.
- If you want stronger impact, rename the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner alignment with the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists the same platforms plus related execution skills.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight versus your enterprise profile; remove it if you need to tighten seniority positioning.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modernize the phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Replace with a tighter, more current list: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent work; if retained, place last or label as **legacy support**
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. **supports Drupal microsites, analytics deployment and workflow automation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears under Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place only
- **API integrations** and automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and “Automation & Workflow Systems”; avoid repeating the same terms across sections

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and trim low-value collaboration tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp.”
- Remove Slack, Teams unless this section is meant to include everyday collaboration tools; they dilute the technical signal.
- If accurate, add a qualifier to show depth: “Built and managed workflows in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier” or “Workflow design, automation and project operations.”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” to better match your recent leadership scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp may be implied by cross-department planning in recent NACo roles, so keep only the strongest/current tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but as written it’s just a tool list and undersells scope. It should signal enterprise email/engagement platform ownership without repeating newsletter details already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level: **Enterprise email marketing, member communications and journey orchestration platforms**
- Keep platform names only here; let work experience carry audience size, newsletter volume and channel leadership metrics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 roles.
- “Engagement Systems” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere; “CRM & Engagement Platforms” is clearer and more specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to signal level of use or business impact. Since recent NACo work already proves these tools, this item should be tighter and more capability-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the flat list with grouped phrasing: “Analytics & BI: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Swap generic nouns for stronger capability terms: “SEO analysis” instead of “SEO,” “Experimentation” instead of “A/B testing,” “Executive dashboarding” instead of “Dashboarding”
- Consider final version: “Analytics & BI: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • Optimization: SEO analysis, experimentation, executive dashboarding”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to outcomes from recent roles (e.g., reporting for 3.5M annual page views, improved decision-making)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; keep one detailed and make the other shorter or broader.
- “Dashboarding” is already implied by Looker Studio and Power BI, so only keep it if reframed as a business capability.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with concrete outputs rather than team/operations language repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function.”
- Add clearer scope and outputs: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia production; contributed to a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring video updates.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” only if that support was meaningful and sustained.
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, website size, or frequency of weekly updates.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with the 2018–2024 roles; keep this entry centered on hands-on production and team formation.
- “Weekly video updates” appears again in the next role; distinguish this as launching or early production support if accurate.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete project outputs, while keeping the rest concise.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a specific deliverable if possible (e.g., videos, reports, campaign assets, stakeholder resources).
- If available, add scale or impact: number of episodes, internal/external audience, cross-team partners, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.
- Consider a two-part structure: research/program support first, digital/media achievement second.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language here.
- Since later entries already show video and digital leadership, this item should mainly establish the podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep workflow/production capabilities in experience or topline skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative Software**
